title: Car shakes when braking
h1: Why does my car shake when I brake?
metaDesc: Car shakes when braking? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's the rotors, calipers or suspension, how urgent it is, and what to tell your mechanic.
synonyms: shaking when braking at high speed
wheel shakes when i hit the brakes
intro: A shake or pulse when you brake often comes from the brake rotors no longer being perfectly even. That's common, but it is still a brake problem worth having checked, and a shake that comes with a soft pedal, grinding or a burning smell needs attention right away. Answer the questions below to see how urgent yours may be and what could be behind it.
safety: If the brake pedal feels soft, sinks toward the floor, or the red brake warning light comes on, stop driving and get help.
If you smell burning or see smoke from a wheel, pull over safely and let the brakes cool. Don't keep driving.
If you hear loud metal-on-metal grinding when braking, stop driving it. Your brakes may be worn through.

q_warning.q: Besides the shaking, do any of these happen?
q_warning.help: These are signs the brakes themselves aren't working properly, which matters more than the shake.

opts.a: The pedal feels soft or sinks, or the car pulls hard to one side when braking
Loud grinding or scraping, like metal on metal
A burning smell, smoke, or one wheel is much hotter than the others
None of these, the brakes stop the car normally

q_where.q: Where do you feel the shaking most when you brake?
q_where.help: Front brake problems usually show up in the steering wheel and brake pedal. Rear brake problems are felt more in the seat or the whole car.

opts.a: In the brake pedal, which pulses up and down
In the seat or through the whole car
The car shakes when I'm not braking too, it just gets worse when I brake

q_when.q: Which of these fits the steering wheel shake best?

opts.a: It's worst when braking from highway speed, and fine otherwise
It started right after new brakes, new tires or a tire rotation
The car also clunks over bumps, wanders, or the steering feels loose

result.title: The braking system may be failing. Don't drive it
result.now: Park the car and have it towed to a shop, or have a mobile mechanic come to you.
if: If the red brake warning light is on or the brake fluid is low, that adds to the evidence of a leak or worn brakes. Don't top it off and drive.
Not finding a leak doesn't mean the brakes are safe. Fluid can leak inside the system or somewhere you can't see.
If the car pulls hard to one side, a caliper or brake hose on one side may be stuck or failing.
If you smell burning or see smoke from a wheel, keep away from it until it cools.
result.why: A soft or sinking pedal can mean the brakes don't have enough hydraulic pressure to stop the car, and a hard pull can mean one side is braking much more than the other. Either can get worse without warning, so the car shouldn't be driven until it's inspected.

causes.name: Brake fluid leak
causes.clues: A low fluid level, a wet spot near a wheel, or a soft pedal that keeps getting worse.

causes.name: Stuck or seized caliper on one side
causes.clues: The car pulls hard to one side, and that wheel gets very hot.

causes.name: Air in the brake lines or failing master cylinder
causes.clues: A spongy pedal, or a pedal that slowly sinks while you hold it down at a stop.

you: With the engine off, check the brake fluid level in the reservoir under the hood.
Look behind each wheel and under the car for wet, oily spots.
shop: Brake system inspection on a lift

result.title: The brake pads may be worn down to metal
result.now: Avoid driving the car. Have it towed, or have a mobile mechanic inspect the brakes where it's parked.
if: If the grinding only happened once after the car sat in the rain, it may have been surface rust. If it happens again, or you're unsure, have the brakes inspected before driving further.
If the brake pedal also feels soft or sinks, the red brake light is on, or the car pulls hard, don't drive it at all.
If you smell burning or see smoke from a wheel, keep away from it until it cools.
result.why: Grinding when braking often means the pad material is gone and metal is scraping the rotor. That can reduce braking power and quickly gouges the rotor, which causes shaking. The longer it goes, the worse and more costly the damage. A shop will measure the pads and rotors to confirm what is worn.

causes.name: Brake pads worn down
causes.clues: A squeal for weeks before the grinding started, or a long time since the last brake job.

causes.name: Rock or debris caught in the brake
causes.clues: The grinding started suddenly after driving on gravel.

causes.name: Rusted or damaged rotor
causes.clues: The car sat for a long time, or the rotor surface looks rough and grooved.

you: Look through the wheel spokes at the brake pad and rotor for deep grooves or very thin pads.

result.title: A brake may be sticking and overheating
result.now: Pull over safely and let the brakes cool. Then have the car towed or have a mobile mechanic check it.
if: If you see flames or heavy smoke, get away from the car and call for help.
If the pedal feels soft, sinks, or braking takes much more force, don't drive it. Overheated brakes can fade.
Even if the smell happened once after a long downhill stretch and goes away after cooling, have the brakes inspected before driving far. A brake that overheats once can do it again.
result.why: A burning smell or one very hot wheel can mean a brake isn't releasing fully. The constant rubbing overheats the pad and rotor, which causes shaking and can fade the brakes or, in rare cases, start a fire.

causes.name: Sticking or seized caliper
causes.clues: One wheel is much hotter than the others, and the car may pull to that side.

causes.name: Stuck caliper slide pins
causes.clues: Uneven pad wear, with one pad much thinner than the other on the same wheel.

causes.name: Parking brake not fully releasing
causes.clues: The heat and smell come from a rear wheel.

you: Make sure the parking brake is fully released.
After the car cools, carefully hold your hand near (not on) each wheel to compare heat.

result.title: The front brake rotors may be uneven, often called warped
result.now: If the brake pedal feels soft or sinks, the red brake warning light comes on, or you hear grinding, stop driving and have it towed. Otherwise: Have the brakes inspected within the next few days. Until then, allow extra stopping distance and avoid hard braking from high speed.
if: If the shaking gets suddenly worse, or the pedal starts feeling soft or sinking, stop driving and have it towed.
If you hear grinding, smell burning, or the red brake warning light comes on, stop driving and have it towed.
If the pads are also low, the shop will usually measure the rotors to decide whether they can be resurfaced or need replacing.
result.why: When the brake rotor's surface becomes uneven, the pads grab harder on some spots than others as it spins. You feel that as a pulse in the pedal or a shake in the steering wheel, usually worst when slowing from higher speeds. It's common and fixable, but it tends to get worse, can lengthen stopping distances and wears the pads unevenly. A shop will usually measure the rotors and check the calipers before deciding on a repair.

causes.name: Uneven rotor thickness or pad deposits
causes.clues: A steady pulse in the pedal that gets worse when braking from highway speed.

causes.name: Overheated rotors
causes.clues: The car does a lot of towing, mountain driving or hard braking.

causes.name: Sticking caliper
causes.clues: One wheel runs hotter than the others, or the pads are wearing unevenly.

you: Note whether the shake is in the pedal, the steering wheel, or both.
Note the speed at which it's most noticeable.
shop: Pad thickness and wear pattern check

result.title: The rear rotors or brake drums may be uneven
result.now: If the brake pedal feels soft or sinks, the red brake warning light comes on, or you hear grinding, stop driving and have it towed. Otherwise: Have the brakes inspected within the next few days. Mention that you feel it in the seat rather than the steering wheel. Allow extra stopping distance until then.
if: If the pedal starts to feel soft or sinks, or you hear grinding, stop driving and have it towed.
If you smell burning, see smoke from a rear wheel, or the red brake warning light comes on, stop driving and have it checked before driving further.
If the parking brake also feels weak or grabby, ask the shop to check it at the same time.
result.why: Rear brake problems don't usually reach the steering wheel, so you feel them in the seat or the whole car instead. Rear rotors can become uneven like the fronts, and drum brakes can go slightly out of round.

causes.name: Uneven rear rotors
causes.clues: A shudder through the seat when braking, especially from higher speeds.

causes.name: Out-of-round rear brake drums
causes.clues: The car has drum brakes at the rear, and the shudder is worse at lower speeds.

causes.name: Sticking rear caliper or parking brake
causes.clues: One rear wheel runs hotter, or there's a burning smell after driving.

you: Check whether the shake changes if you brake gently versus firmly.

result.title: Worn suspension parts or a tire problem may be making it shake
result.now: Get the front suspension, tires and brakes inspected within the next few days. Drive gently and avoid highways until then.
if: If you see a bulge on a tire, or the steering suddenly feels much looser, don't drive it. Use the spare or have it towed.
If the brake pedal feels soft or sinks, or the red brake light comes on, stop driving and have it towed.
If the shake only happens when braking, the rotors are the more likely cause.
result.why: Braking shifts the car's weight forward and puts extra load on the front suspension. Worn joints, bushings or a damaged tire that cause a mild shake normally can feel much worse when you brake, and loose steering parts are a safety risk. A shop will usually inspect the suspension, tires and brakes together to find which is responsible.

causes.name: Worn control arm bushings or ball joints
causes.clues: Clunks over bumps, or the steering wheel jerks when braking.

causes.name: Worn tie rod ends
causes.clues: Loose or wandering steering.

causes.name: Out-of-balance or damaged tire
causes.clues: A shake at highway speed that's there even without braking, or a visible bulge.

you: Look over each tire for bulges, cuts or uneven wear.

result.title: It may be related to the recent work
result.now: If the brake pedal feels soft or sinks, the red brake warning light comes on, or you hear grinding, stop driving and have it towed. Otherwise: Go back to the shop that did the work within a day or two. Let them know what you feel and ask them to check the wheel lug nuts, rotors and balance. Shops want to hear about this and it's usually a quick check.
if: If you hear clicking or clunking from a wheel, or feel a wobble, stop driving. A wheel may be loose. Have it towed.
If the brake pedal feels soft or sinks, or you smell burning, stop driving and have it checked before going further.
If it was a brake job, new pads sometimes need a proper break-in. Ask the shop if that was done.
result.why: Lug nuts that aren't tightened evenly can distort a rotor and cause a shake under braking. New rotors can also have a slight runout, or a tire may have lost a balance weight. These are common and a shop can check them quickly.

causes.name: Uneven or loose lug nuts
causes.clues: The shake started right after a tire change or rotation.

causes.name: Rotor runout or rust between the rotor and hub
causes.clues: New rotors were installed, and the shake started right away.

causes.name: Missing wheel balance weight
causes.clues: The steering wheel also shakes at highway speed without braking.

you: Check that none of the lug nuts look loose or missing.
